article:what-is-oes.title: What OES is
article:what-is-oes.content:
# What OES is

OES (Open Education Standards) is a set of open specifications for
education content: courses, practice sets, questions, articles, video
lessons and reference documents, plus a format for packaging and sharing
them.

## Plain files you can keep in git

Every OES document is a JSON file, with longer prose in Markdown. Nothing
needs a database or a server: a course is a folder you can put in a git
repository, review in a pull request, and host anywhere that serves files.
Who may read it is up to wherever you host it.

## Seven specs that compose

| Spec | Describes |
|---|---|
| OCF | A course: modules, lessons, and the items in each lesson |
| OPF | A practice set: an ordered list of questions |
| OQF | A single question, in one of 11 types |
| OAF | A written article |
| OVF | A video lesson around a video hosted elsewhere |
| ORF | A reference document, such as a PDF or a paper |
| OPK | A package: a named, versioned unit you can share |

A course doesn't contain its lessons; it points at them. Every reference
is either a `path` to a file next to it or a URL to one hosted elsewhere,
so the same question can appear in several practice sets.

## Content, not learner data

OES describes what a learner studies. Progress, attempts and grades are
deliberately left out: those belong to whatever app the learner uses.

## Read more

The full specifications are at
[open-education-standards.github.io/oes](https://open-education-standards.github.io/oes/).

article:first-question.title: Write your first question
article:first-question.content:
# Write your first question

A question is one `question.json` file. Here is a complete multiple-choice
question:

```json
{
  "oqf_version": "0.2.0",
  "id": "capital-of-france",
  "type": "mcq",
  "title": "Capital of France",
  "statement": "What is the capital of France?",
  "type_config": {
    "options": [
      { "id": "a", "content": "Paris" },
      { "id": "b", "content": "Lyon" }
    ],
    "answer": "a"
  }
}
```

- `type` picks one of 11 question types, such as `mcq`, `fill_blank`,
  `code` or `essay`.
- `statement` is the question itself, in Markdown. A long statement can
  live in its own `statement.md` instead.
- `type_config` holds what that type needs: here, the options and the
  answer.

## Practice or graded

With the answer inline, as above, the question suits self-practice: an
app can check a learner's answer straight away. For a graded question,
move the answer into a separate file named by `answer_key`. An app
showing the question to a learner then never receives the answer.

## Put it in a set

A practice set (`set.json`) lists questions in order and gives each its
points. Points belong to the set, not the question, so the same question
can be worth different amounts in different sets.

## Check it

The `oes` command line tool validates documents and checks that every
reference resolves:

```bash
npx @inklyre/oes-lint lint ./my-course
```

question:which-spec.title: Which spec describes a question
question:which-spec.statement: Which OES spec describes a single question?
question:which-spec.explanation: OQF, the Open Question Format, describes one question. OPF describes a practice set, which lists questions.

question:graded-answers.title: Where a graded question keeps its answer
question:graded-answers.statement: Where does a graded question keep its answer, so that an app showing it to a learner never receives the answer?

options.content: In a separate file named by `answer_key`

question:graded-answers.explanation: A graded question moves its answer into a separate file named by `answer_key`. With the answer inline, the question is meant for self-practice.

question:out-of-scope.title: What OES leaves out
question:out-of-scope.statement: What does OES deliberately leave out of its documents?
question:out-of-scope.explanation: OES describes content. Progress, attempts and grades are learner data, which belongs to the app the learner uses.
